The OSHA 300 Log requires recording cases involving days away from work with a check mark in the space for cases involving days away and an entry of the number of calendar days away from work in the number of days column [2]. When a single injury or illness involves both days away from work and days of restricted work activity, the total number of days for each must be entered [4]. Counting begins the day after the incident occurs, and the day of injury is not counted [1][4]. The employer may stop counting days away from work or days of restricted work activity once the total of either or the combination of both reaches 180 days [1][4].
